items.description: argo-cd D7 stands and carries Ruling D1 as an amendment. The notification is the event, and its expiry sends no resolve. The Prometheus rule is the standing state. The standing failed-sync alert covers auto-synced apps only, and the standing degraded alert covers every app.
items.rationale: argo-cd/decisions.md D7 stands and carries a dated, attributed amendment (2026-09-25, operator, slice 028 Ruling D1; ANS-47) that says: the notification is the failure event; the engine sets no end time so Alertmanager expires it and the expiry sends no 'resolved'; the standing state comes from Prometheus rules over Argo CD's application metrics and resolves on recovery; the failed-sync alert covers auto-synced apps only (Argo CD's own, D3, keeps the event alone) while the degraded alert covers every app; the accepted trade-off is two messages per failure. Read against Ruling D1: every point present, no other decision changed (git log -- argo-cd/decisions.md: e03a4d8 is the only slice-028 touch).

items.area: R4 — ANS-96 promote re-run finishes a tagless release
items.description: KubeCoderDeploy Jenkinsfile.promote: a re-run can finish a release whose tag push failed. When prd is already at the commit and no release tag points at it, the job writes D48's annotated release tag instead of refusing, numbered after the build that writes it, and nothing else changes.
items.rationale: Owed to the operator after ../KubeCoderDeploy is pushed (after a `git pull --rebase`: origin/main moved by two Build-Main pin commits that touch config/*/values.yaml only). Earned offline by reading Jenkinsfile.promote: when origin/prd equals the resolved commit and `git tag --list 'release-*' --points-at <sha>` is empty, recordOnly is set, Retagging the images and Advancing prd are skipped, and Recording the release writes release-<this build> as an annotated tag whose message says the commit was already on prd; the non-fast-forward and existing-release-tag checks still run. The tag lookup was witnessed in a scratch git repo (annotated release tags on two commits, a non-release tag as noise, and a fresh clone): it lists exactly the release-* tags on the commit, none where there is none. The Jenkins run is what remains. Settles with: run KubeCoder/Promote with `commit=<prd's tip>` while a release tag sits on it and see the refusal 'prd is already at <sha>, released as release-N: nothing to promote'; the record-only path needs a tagless prd tip (an actual failed recording, or deleting the latest release-N tag on origin by hand, which is the operator's call), then `commit=<that sha>` writes release-<build>.
